thread:
Maya (CS): ACME reports failing requests when they try to call rerank and embeddings in a single flow. They only see 403s intermittently. Can someone triage?

ACME App: We're seeing 403s for some users. Payloads that do only text-gen work fine. Example error: `{"error":"forbidden","message":"insufficient_scope: embeddings"}`. Happening since yesterday afternoon. No changes on our side AFAIK.

Akash (Support): Thanks — can you paste the exact API call you used (headers + minimal body)? Also curious if you're using the SDK or raw REST, and whether you create the key via the Console or SSO.

ACME App: Using raw REST. Header: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***`. Body snippet: ```json
{ "model": "open-embed-1", "input": "..." }
```
Request to `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings`.

Maya (CS): Do you have a bunch of keys? Usually this looks like a token missing the embeddings scope (or using an older key after rotate).

ACME App: We actually have a few keys — one for prod, one for a worker pool. The worker pool does rerank + embeddings. The prod-only path is fine. Could be the worker token.

Leo (Platform): Can you check the response body for `required_scopes` or any meta? We added a small hint to 403 bodies that lists missing scopes in the last quarter.

ACME App: Full 403 body: `{"error":"insufficient_scope","missing_scopes":["embeddings.read","rerank.execute"],"message":"token lacks required scopes"}`.

Akash (Support): That's pretty definitive — token in that request doesn't have `embeddings.read` or `rerank.execute`. Two possibilities: (1) they rotated keys and the old key was limited, (2) they generated a key via SSO with restricted scopes.

ACME App: We rotated keys last week as part of CI changes. The new keys are generated by a CI job that hits our org's SSO-provisioning endpoint. Could provisioning be stripping scopes?

Sam (SRE): If keys are created via SSO/OAuth provisioning, the client app can request scopes. If the provisioning service supplies a subset, you'd get this. Akash — can you check audit logs to see which key was used for the failing requests?

Akash (Support): On it. Pulling logs... `curl "https://audit.redwood.ai/v1/keys?created_by=acme-ci"` gave a list. I grep'd for the key id prefix from the Authorization header and matched it to `key_id: k_9a7c-prod-worker`. That key was issued with scopes: `inference.generate` only. No embeddings or rerank.

Maya (CS): That matches the error. Why did the CI provisioning job request only `inference.generate`? Maybe someone hard-coded a scopes list in the provisioning template.

ACME App: We had a minimal-scope policy for CI keys to limit risk. But our worker actually needs embeddings + rerank for the reranking pipeline. Oops.

Leo (Platform): Two action items: (A) short-term: create a new key with the proper scopes (embeddings.read, rerank.execute, inference.generate) and update the worker env var; (B) long-term: change the provisioning template and add a validation step that asserts required pipeline scopes.

Akash (Support): To unblock quickly, here's a repro and fix steps for the customer: 
1) Reproduce: `curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" -H "Authorization: Bearer <their-key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"test"}'` -> returns 403 with `missing_scopes`.
2) Inspect key scopes from Console or Audit API: `GET /v1/keys/<key_id>` -> `"scopes":[...]`.
3) Generate new key: Console -> Create API Key -> check boxes `Embeddings:read`, `Rerank:execute`, `Inference:generate` (or via Admin API `POST /v1/keys {"scopes":["embeddings.read","rerank.execute","inference.generate"]}` ).
4) Deploy updated key to worker, restart, confirm success.

ACME App: We created a new key with the three scopes and swapped it in the worker, restarted. Rerank pipeline calls succeed now. Thanks! 

Maya (CS): Great. Two follow-ups: (1) Akash, can you mark this as "scope-misgrant" and include the provisioning template line that only requested `inference.generate` so ACME can update their CI? (2) Leo/Sam, can we make the API error text more actionable? The missing_scopes field is helpful but customers sometimes miss it in large log streams. Maybe add `hint: "create key with scopes: embeddings.read,rerank.execute"` when those are missing?

Leo (Platform): We intentionally keep 403 messages generic for security, but the missing_scopes array is okay. We can add a short `hint` string for cases where the missing scopes are a small, known set (embeddings/rerank/inference). I'll put a short RFC and see if legal/security is fine.

Sam (SRE): Also suggest instrumentation: emit a metric `auth.missing_scopes` with tag listing the missing scope names (not the key id) so we can alert when a single scope dominates.

Akash (Support): Filed ticket CS-1123 to annotate the customer's case and include repro steps and the audit log snippet. I also provided the exact `curl` commands and the Console screenshot showing the new key scopes.

ACME App: FYI — the CI provisioning template had this line: `scopes: ["inference.generate"]` (we'll change it). Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Maya (CS): Closing loop: customer is unblocked, root cause = CI key created with too-narrow scopes. Recommend adding an internal playbook step for scope checklist when adding new worker services.

DeployBot: Deployed update to worker cluster (acme-worker-1) using new env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY` at 2026-04-18T15:32:10Z :white_check_mark:

Akash (Support): Marking thread resolved. Will follow up with scope-tenancy guide link and automated provisioning checklist. :thumbsup:
